strings.help.check: Choose a container to see the audio codecs allowed by the app.
strings.help.workflow:
Drop a video into the window or add files and folders under Sources. Folders include subfolders. Remove and Clear edit the list. The Audio tracks tab shows streams for the selected file.
Choose an output folder under File. Click the active settings at the bottom left and try Auto with your preferred language, AAC, video COPY and MKV. Press F5 to start. Use Analyze only for a trial measurement.
The right side shows active jobs, total progress and time remaining. The log toolbar controls scrolling, copying, saving and clearing. Open the output folder at the bottom left.
strings.help.targets:
Start with a loudness preset such as Streaming / Web at −16 LUFS or EBU R128 at −23 LUFS. Choose Custom for individual targets.
I controls integrated loudness across the track. −16 LUFS sounds louder on average than −23 LUFS. TP limits signal peaks in dBTP. LRA sets the target range between quiet and loud passages.
strings.help.tracks:
Auto uses the first matching language track, falling back to the first audio track. This works well with mixed DEU, ENG and UND music videos. UND means the language is unspecified.
Preferred language only processes all matches. If none match, the log lists the filter and available tags. This mode can move matching tracks to the front. All tracks normalizes every audio stream. Other audio streams are copied during export.
strings.help.cache:
Analyze only measures selected audio tracks without creating an output video. Turn it off to export.
Measurements are stored under analysis-cache in the data folder, e.g. Film.mkv.txt. With the same source, track, target and FFmpeg build, an export can reuse the measurement after a codec or container change. Delete the matching TXT to repeat the measurement. Variants may be in subfolders.
strings.help.codecs:
AAC suits MP4 and widely supported playback. E-AC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) suits surround sound, for example on a TV. Check support on your player.
Opus compresses efficiently and is exported at 48 kHz, for example in WebM. PCM 24-bit stores normalized samples uncompressed at the source sample rate, useful for editing at the cost of larger files.
Compressed codecs have an audio bitrate in kbit/s. Higher values give the encoder more room. For PCM the channel count, sample rate and bit depth determine the data rate.
strings.help.containers:
MKV is flexible for films with multiple tracks. MP4 is common for sharing, MOV for editing and TS for transport streams. Auto follows the source and changes the container for certain combinations. Auto can retain AVI and M4V.
WebM needs Opus and video COPY. Source video must be VP8, VP9 or AV1. Copied audio must be Opus or Vorbis and subtitles WebVTT. For other containers too, copied streams and the target player must support the combination.
strings.help.video:
COPY preserves the picture without quality loss. Choose an encoder to recompress it. H.264 suits widespread playback, HEVC efficient compression. x264 and x265 use the CPU. Hardware options depend on platform, GPU and FFmpeg (NVENC, AMF, VAAPI or VideoToolbox).
NVENC ranges from P7 (higher quality, slower) through P4 (balanced) to P1 (faster). AMF has its own presets. QP 14–27 controls quality, with smaller numbers usually giving larger files. Bitrate sets a budget in Mbit/s, such as 8 Mbit/s or a custom value. The dialog shows the options for the selected encoder.
strings.help.jobs:
Auto chooses parallel job counts. Reduce them if the CPU, GPU or disk is saturated. Resume skips finished files on the next run. An interrupted encode starts again.
Overwrite replaces the original after successful encoding in the same container. Its timestamp can be preserved. Changing container creates a separate file. Use a separate output folder for trials.
Choose a completion action such as sleep or shutdown. Notifications and startup update checks have separate switches.
strings.help.paths:
FFmpeg measures and encodes. FFprobe reads duration, codecs and language tags. If either is missing, select its executable in Paths & Tools. This page also contains the output, temporary and data folders. Resume history can be cleared separately from the analysis cache.
Under Video & Encoder choose the default suffix, your own suffix or none. It goes before the extension. For separate output in the source folder, an empty suffix falls back to the default to protect the source.
strings.help.profiles:
Save a working combination under a name in Profiles. Select it there for the next run. The loudness preset under Normalization controls only measurement targets.
Settings lets you change language and theme, create a language template and reload translations. Help → Quick tips switches hover guidance On or Off.
strings.help.diagnostics:
For a failed run, read the detail line for the file in the log. For ERROR_NO_MATCHING_AUDIO inspect the Audio tracks tab and select Auto to fall back to track 1. For container errors check copied streams as well.
Info contains build details, diagnostics, changes, update checks, project page and data folder. To report an issue, save the log and include the settings used.
strings.tip.start: Start the run with the active settings shown at the bottom left (F5).
strings.tip.remove: Remove the selection from the list. Files stay on disk.
strings.tip.folder: Add supported videos from this folder and its subfolders.
strings.tip.files: Select one or more videos for this run.
strings.tip.cancel: Stop active jobs. Completed outputs are kept.
strings.tip.i: Average loudness over the track. −16 LUFS is louder than −23 LUFS.
strings.tip.tp: Peak ceiling. A negative value leaves headroom below full scale.
strings.tip.lra: Target loudness range between quiet and loud passages.
strings.tip.lang: Auto prefers this language and falls back to track 1. The strict filter requires a match.
strings.tip.audio: AAC for common players, E-AC3 for surround, Opus for WebM or PCM 24-bit for editing.
strings.tip.rate: More kbit/s gives the audio encoder more room and increases file size.
strings.tip.preset: A slower preset gives the encoder more time to compress the picture.
strings.tip.video: COPY preserves the picture. Re-encoding lets you control video size.
strings.tip.vRate: QP controls picture quality. Target bitrate controls the data budget in Mbit/s.
strings.tip.tools: Leave empty for automatic discovery or select the executable path.
strings.tip.format: Choose a container for all streams. The guide lists compatible audio codecs.

strings.trackmode.all.hint: Slower, because every audio track is analyzed and re-encoded.
strings.trackmode.preferred_only.hint: Usually faster than “All tracks”. Only {lang} tracks are normalized; other tracks stay unchanged.

strings.audio.format_hint: Opus uses 48 kHz. PCM stores normalized audio uncompressed at 24 bits and at the source sample rate.
